Interactive heatmaps: a web page to explore and select from

Source: R/heat_map_html.R
heat_map_html.Rd

heat_map_html() writes a heatmap to a self-contained web page - one HTML file, with nothing to install and nothing loaded from the internet - in which the heatmap can be explored and its rows and columns picked out:

Usage

heat_map_html(
  x,
  ...,
  file = NULL,
  width = 7,
  height = 7,
  format = c("auto", "svg", "png"),
  res = 150,
  title = NULL,
  max_cells = 1e+06,
  browse = interactive()
)

Arguments

x

a heatmap (an object of class heat_map, e.g. from heat_map, heat_map_dot, heat_map_cor or heat_map_composition), or data to draw with heat_map() and the arguments in ....

...

arguments of heat_map when x is data, or settings that replace those of the heatmap x (e.g. a new title).

file

the HTML file to write, or NULL (default) for a temporary file.

width, height

the size of the heatmap in inches, 7 by 7 by default; on the page it is shown at its width (96 pixels per inch) or narrower to fit, and zooms from there.

format

"svg" or "png", or "auto" (default): SVG when R can write it (with cairo), else PNG.

res

the resolution of PNG images in pixels per inch, 150 by default.

title

the title of the page, by default that of the heatmap.

max_cells

the largest number of cells whose values are written to the page, 1 million by default; larger heatmaps show the names of their rows and columns only, which keeps the page small.

browse

logical, whether to open the page, by default in interactive sessions.

Value

an object of class heat_map_html, invisibly: the path of the page (file), with its size. Printing it opens the page.

Details

  • hovering over a cell shows its row, column and value (and the value before scaling, its size, clusters and annotations), and hovering over a label shows the row or column;

  • clicking a cell or a row's label selects (or unselects) the row, and clicking a column's label the column; dragging a box across cells, labels or dendrograms selects every row and column in it (Alt unselects them) - e.g. the genes of a cluster, picked off the dendrogram;

  • the selected rows and columns are listed beside the heatmap, to copy (one name per line, e.g. for features) or to download with their values as a CSV file;

  • a search box highlights the rows and columns whose names contain the text (Enter selects them), and the heatmap zooms (the buttons, or Ctrl or Cmd with the mouse wheel) for large heatmaps.

The heatmap is drawn as it is by heat_map - an SVG image by default, so it stays sharp when zoomed, or a PNG image - with its values alongside, and the page works offline and can be shared as one file. In an interactive session the page opens in the viewer of RStudio or Positron, or in a web browser; in R Markdown and Quarto documents rendered as HTML it is embedded where it is printed.

See also

heat_map, heat_map_data

Author

Dillon Hammill (dillon.hammill21@gmail.com)

Examples

# \donttest{
page <- heat_map_html(
  mtcars,
  scale = "column",
  tree = "both",
  tree_cut_y = 3,
  title = "mtcars",
  file = file.path(tempdir(), "mtcars.html"),
  browse = FALSE
)
#> Applying range scaling to each column...
page
#> Interactive heatmap: /tmp/RtmpbrSn7b/mtcars.html

# A heatmap drawn before, with a new title
grDevices::pdf(NULL)
hm <- heat_map(iris[1:40, 1:4], scale = "column", popup = FALSE)
#> Applying range scaling to each column...
grDevices::dev.off()
#> agg_record_18da5c90a41c 
#>                       2 
heat_map_html(hm, title = "iris", browse = FALSE)
# }
